title: Naturality of normalized finite Verdier shift components
statement: For the finite coherent rational Verdier data of def-sf-common-stage-verdier-data, there exists a family of exact integer CommShift structures on the finite dual functors such that the explicit shiftComponent maps are natural in each integer degree on common-stage quotient morphisms. finiteRestrictionShift is transport of the finite composite shift along the specified descendedComparison. shiftComponent cancels the opposite-inclusion shift from this transported shift at the original stage of each pair. The conclusion asserts only exactness of the finite shifts and naturality of these explicit components, not a global coherent CommShift or compatibility of its finite comparisons.

source.place: Coefficient transport: shift coherence for the explicit common-stage dual

proof.text: Construct the finite shift maps by signed reindexing of the internal-Hom complex. Their evaluations are the tensor-Hom shift transposes, and the cone calculation proves exactness for these finite shifts.

Use the normalized scalar-extension evaluation equation. Transpose the evaluation shift square to show that the actual beta maps commute with the chosen finite shifts. For a pair arrow represented over a common finite overfield, apply finite naturality there and the beta squares at its ends. The finiteMorphism representative formula is conjugation by these same beta maps. This gives the displayed equation; tower coherence ensures it is independent of the quotient representative.

proof_origin.place: K6: finite internal-Hom shift normalization and common-stage arrow naturality only

lean.statement:
theorem finite_shift_naturality (F : Finite D l hl Ω X)
    (hF : FiniteCoherent D l hl Ω X F) :
    ∃ t : ∀ E : AlgebraicallyClosedCoefficients.Index l Ω,
        (F.datum E).dual.CommShift ℤ,
      (∀ E : AlgebraicallyClosedCoefficients.Index l Ω,
        letI := t E
        (F.datum E).dual.IsTriangulated) ∧
      ∀ (n : ℤ) (P Q : (generalAlgebraicallyClosedConstructibleCategory l Ω X)ᵒᵖ)
        (f : P ⟶ Q),
        (descendedDual D l hl Ω X F hF).map (f⟦n⟧') ≫
          (shiftComponent D l hl Ω X F hF t n Q).hom =
        (shiftComponent D l hl Ω X F hF t n P).hom ≫
          ((descendedDual D l hl Ω X F hF).map f)⟦n⟧'
